Its moral distance can be chilly, but the precise treatment of desire and power shows the literary possibilities of fantasy without spectacular supernatural machinery.

works.title: The Etched City
works.form_reported: Novel.
works.tradition: New Weird/literary dark fantasy; Australia.
works.rationale: A harsh journey opens into a city where art, faith and transformation disturb the apparent solidity of everyday life. Bishop's imagery is unusually forceful, and the book resists reducing its strangeness to a single explanation. Its diffuse movement limits narrative satisfaction, but the atmosphere and intellectual unease linger.

works.title: The Empress of Salt and Fortune
works.form_reported: Novella; other Singing Hills books excluded.
works.tradition: Archival and political fantasy; Vietnamese-American writing.
works.rationale: Objects and remembered details gradually overturn the public account of an empress's life. Vo makes the act of listening a source of narrative tension, giving sidelined labor and testimony real power. Its compression is a major strength; the shorter history of reception makes its all-time position necessarily provisional.

works.title: Spear
works.form_reported: Short novel/novella; marketed as a novella, with award-category treatment varying.
works.tradition: Queer Arthurian fantasy; British-American writing.
works.rationale: Peretur's growing knowledge of herself gives the familiar quest a fresh emotional center. Landscape, bodily skill and rhythmic prose make the world immediate without extensive exposition. The reworking is compact and assured, though its enduring influence has had little time to become clear compared with older Arthurian classics.

works.title: Where the Wild Ladies Are (Obachan-tachi no iru tokoro / おばちゃんたちのいるところ)
works.form_reported: Connected author collection of seventeen stories.
works.tradition: Feminist literary ghost stories/modern kaidan; Japan.
works.rationale: Traditional ghosts acquire jobs, desires and practical relationships with contemporary women. Matsuda's wit exposes the persistence of gendered labor beneath apparently modern freedom. The interconnections give the collection more than a succession of reversals, while its tonal lightness makes the social criticism unexpectedly persistent.

works.title: Cursed Bunny (저주토끼)
works.form_reported: Author collection of ten stories; mixed fantasy, horror and science fiction. The collection is judged as a whole, with its supernatural and impossible-body stories central to inclusion.
works.tradition: Grotesque fantastic and speculative social horror; South Korea.
works.rationale: Absurd bodies and malicious objects turn economic and gendered pressures into immediate threats. Chung's directness can make the tales feel brutally simple, yet their shifts between ridiculous and terrifying are highly effective. Unevenness and the mixed-genre contents limit the claim, but the strongest stories have considerable originality and force.

works.title: The City of Dreaming Books (Die Stadt der Träumenden Bücher)
works.form_reported: Novel, with the author's illustrations; later Bookholm/Zamonia books and graphic adaptations excluded.
works.tradition: Comic/bibliophilic fantasy; Germany.
works.rationale: The book trade becomes a literal ecosystem of danger, appetite and artistic ambition. Moers's verbal and visual exuberance serves a surprisingly dark view of how culture is manufactured and consumed. The profusion can become self-indulgent, but the sustained imaginative play and distinctive setting create unusual reading pleasure.

works.title: Brave Story (ブレイブ・ストーリー)
works.form_reported: Prose novel, originally issued in two book volumes; manga and film excluded.
works.tradition: Children's/crossover portal fantasy; Japan.
works.rationale: A child's wish to repair family suffering drives a journey that steadily complicates the idea of rewriting one's fate. The long adventure sometimes follows familiar game-like conventions, but its emotional starting point and growing recognition of others' pain give the quest substance beyond wish fulfillment.

works.title: The Name of the Wind
works.form_reported: Individual novel; The Wise Man's Fear and the unfinished Kingkiller Chronicle are not included.
works.tradition: Retrospective/coming-of-age high fantasy; United States.
works.rationale: Kvothe's self-narration makes talent and the construction of a legend mutually dependent. Music, poverty and learning provide memorable, intimate stakes. The protagonist's exceptionalism and the gap between promises and resolution limit the claim, but the fluency of the voice and sustained narrative attraction justify this individual novel's place.

works.title: The Lies of Locke Lamora
works.form_reported: Individual novel; later Gentleman Bastard books excluded.
works.tradition: Urban/heist fantasy; United States.
works.rationale: A vividly practical criminal world supports an intricate confidence plot and a persuasive chosen family. The dialogue and reversals supply exceptional momentum. Some tonal escalation is heavy-handed, but the novel's distinctive social texture and emotional stakes make it more durable than an ingenious caper alone.

works.title: Mistborn: the original trilogy
works.form_reported: Mistborn/The Final Empire; The Well of Ascension; The Hero of Ages. Later eras and Cosmere works excluded.
works.tradition: Epic/high fantasy with rule-based magic; United States.
works.rationale: The completed trilogy repeatedly reinterprets its own prophecies and assumptions, making the final architecture a substantial pleasure. Its magic supports the plot rather than merely decorating it. Functional prose, repetitive explanation and uneven relationships lower the literary assessment, while inventiveness, closure and strong reader attachment support inclusion.

works.title: Dreams Underfoot
works.form_reported: Nineteen linked Newford stories; later collections and novels excluded.
works.tradition: Contemporary urban/faerie fantasy; Canada.
works.rationale: Repeated characters and places make the city a community of overlapping vulnerabilities. Folklore grows out of music, homelessness, artistic work and everyday encounters. The stories' resolutions are uneven, as contemporary criticism noted, but their cumulative attention to overlooked lives helped give urban fantasy a humane and durable vocabulary.

works.title: Among Others
works.form_reported: Novel.
works.tradition: Liminal/autobiographically inflected fantasy; Welsh-Canadian writing. The status of its magic is intentionally contestable.
works.rationale: A reading life becomes a way of surviving isolation and rebuilding an identity. The diary voice connects disability, family damage and the uncertain presence of fairies. Familiarity with the books discussed enriches the experience but can also narrow it; the emotional precision and ambiguity remain its strongest qualities.

works.title: The Ballad of Black Tom
works.form_reported: Novella.
works.tradition: Revisionary cosmic horror/dark fantasy; United States.
works.rationale: LaValle changes the moral and perceptual center of a Lovecraftian premise, giving ordinary racial terror weight beside cosmic terror. Its brevity makes the reversal sharp and forceful. Dependence on a prior story limits the scale of its originality, but the voice and ethical pressure make it a substantial achievement in its own right.

works.title: Alif the Unseen
works.form_reported: Novel.
works.tradition: Contemporary jinn and cyberpunk fantasy; American writing informed by Middle Eastern life.
works.rationale: Digital surveillance and the interpretive power of stories meet in a lively account of resistance. The jinn are involved in arguments about reading and authority, not merely added as exotic spectacle. Uneven characterization and an overbusy climax temper the assessment, but the central synthesis is inventive and purposeful.

works.title: Redemption in Indigo
works.form_reported: Novel.
works.tradition: Caribbean literary fairy tale drawing partly on a Senegalese tale; Barbados.
works.rationale: An intrusive storyteller turns a domestic departure into a widening account of chance, responsibility and compassion. Lord handles the borrowed folktale structure with warmth and slyness, allowing apparently minor lives to matter. The episodic joins can show, but the narrative voice and humane imagination give the short novel lasting charm.

works.title: Imaro
works.form_reported: Original novel/fix-up, with the 2006 revision identified as an alternative that replaces a story; later Imaro novels excluded.
works.tradition: Sword and soul/African-inspired sword and sorcery; African-American/Canadian writing.
works.rationale: Saunders redirects heroic adventure toward an African-inspired imaginative landscape and an outsider's search for belonging. The action is forceful, though the early fix-up structure and some conventional plotting limit depth. Its historical intervention matters, but it also earns a place through the vitality of its protagonist and setting.

works.title: Novoland: Eagle Flag (Jiuzhou Piaomiao Lu / 九州·缥缈录): original six volumes
works.form_reported: The six original novels/volumes ending with Bao hun, not the shared Novoland universe, other authors' works, later expanded projects or the television adaptation.
works.tradition: Contemporary epic fantasy; China.
works.rationale: The friendships of young would-be heroes give the competing states and historical destinies a human focus. Chinese commentary stresses both the series' cultural significance and the limits of its ambitious shared-world undertaking. Its placement remains comparatively provisional, but it earns inclusion through local reception and character-centered invention, not geographical tokenism.
